body:
Continues: https://github.com/linkml/linkml/pull/2028
Continues: https://github.com/linkml/linkml/pull/2023

OK I AM SO SORRY this has taken several PRs to get right - hopefully it's clear that i am not trying to be sloppy and these are problems caused by CI being weird and hard to test, and then in this case by poetry being *extremely opinionated* to a fault.

## Previously...

In the first edition: we got an empty pull request because using `poetry update` without having the packages installed just shows you all the packages that are being installed without differentiating the packages that are being upgraded.

So, in the second edition: we installed the packages first and then called `poetry update`, which WORKED, but...

## The problem...

... apparently ONLY when the lockfile is only mildly out of date - so we [got this failure](https://github.com/linkml/linkml/actions/runs/8502094392/job/23285824078#step:5:16):

```
pyproject.toml changed significantly since poetry.lock was last generated. Run `poetry lock [--no-update]` to fix the lock file.
```

which is FUNNY because that is what we are TRYING to do.


That turns out to be a new "feature" in 1.8.0 
- https://python-poetry.org/blog/announcing-poetry-1.8.0/#upgrading-warning-about-inconsistent-lockfile-to-an-error
- https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/pull/8737
- https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry/issues/5003

that check looks for any changes in dependencies, source, extras, and dev-dependencies, and groups:
- https://github.com/KotlinIsland/poetry/blob/255290e81b3145814ad9aa37985bc171f576bae4/src/poetry/installation/installer.py#L247
- https://github.com/KotlinIsland/poetry/blob/255290e81b3145814ad9aa37985bc171f576bae4/src/poetry/packages/locker.py#L86
- https://github.com/KotlinIsland/poetry/blob/255290e81b3145814ad9aa37985bc171f576bae4/src/poetry/packages/locker.py#L304

so it would basically always throw that error whenever we care about it in this context.

## This PR

HENCE THE THIRD VERSION:

- run `poetry show` to display dependencies BEFORE updating the lockfile
- update the lockfile
- run `poetry show` to display dependencies AFTER updating the lockfile
- diff the two calls to `show`, and use that in the PR body.

## Further Explanation

The extra stuff in the action:

- `awk '{print $1,$3}'` takes 
```
alabaster                     0.7.13         A configurable sidebar-enabled Sphinx theme
annotated-types               0.6.0          Reusable constraint types to use with typing.Annotated
antlr4-python3-runtime        4.9.3          ANTLR 4.9.3 runtime for Python 3.7
```

down to
```
alabaster 0.7.13
annotated-types 0.6.0
antlr4-python3-runtime 4.9.3
```

- `set +e` turns off failing within any pipe - the `diff` call that uses process substitution apparently returns some nonzero exit status at some point somewhere, even though it works correctly. That's FINE here, we actually don't really care if that step fails anyway - all this extra work is really just to work around the fact that poetry doesn't print an informative diff when it relocks, and it would be nice to see what changed at a glance without having to dig through the lockfile. but if that FAILS then we should still open the PR.
- `diff` normally looks like this:
```diff
33c33
< filelock 3.13.2
---
> filelock 3.13.3
44c44
< ipykernel 6.29.3
---
> ipykernel 6.29.4
64c64
< linkml-runtime 1.7.4
---
> linkml-runtime 1.7.5
```
- which sort of sucks. `diff -y --suppress-common-lines -W 80` looks like this instead:
```
filelock 3.13.2                       | filelock 3.13.3
ipykernel 6.29.3                      | ipykernel 6.29.4
linkml-runtime 1.7.4                  | linkml-runtime 1.7.5
```

which is JUST TABLE-LIKE ENOUGH for markdown to consider it a table if we add a header row.

## Demo

SO we can see this version working here: 
- Action run: https://github.com/sneakers-the-rat/linkml/actions/runs/8513677141
- PR: https://github.com/sneakers-the-rat/linkml/pull/6

Where we can see that my fork ALSO had the same problem as upstream: https://github.com/sneakers-the-rat/linkml/actions/runs/8502394094

so i present this PR ~ somewhat but not entirely convinced ~ that it will actually work this time. 

It will still not trigger tests to run because of [the known issue](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request/blob/main/docs/concepts-guidelines.md#triggering-further-workflow-runs) of [github not triggering workflows from workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/triggering-a-workflow#triggering-a-workflow-from-a-workflow) discussed previously, but it is possible to work around that by manually closing and reopening the PR, or creating a bot account, issuing it a PAT, and using that token in the pull request action step.

thank u for ur patience <3

author: azangru
body: ## Description This PR addresses the following bugs: **1. Genomic sequence wasn't fitting into a single line** This was caused by incorrect handling of the variant that affected the first (or the last) nucleotide of a transcript. For example, the line `return getReverseComplement(sequence).slice(-1 * distanceToSliceStart);` would work correctly if `distanceToSliceStart` is greater than 0 (a string would be sliced from the end); but would work incorrectly if `distanceToSliceStart` is equal to 0 (`.slice(0)` means that the whole string will be returned). We thus ended up with two copies of the same sequence to the right and to the left of the variant; and the result was longer than the available space for the sequence. This is what this variant looks like after the fix: ![localhost_8080_entity-viewer_grch38_variant_21_10649400_rs771244603_allele=0 view=transcript-consequences](https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-client/assets/6834224/7e05cdfd-f5ae-4dab-8979-c896d46d1edc) **2. Variant mark on CDS diagram did not start at 0** For a variant that starts at the first nucleotide of the CDS, the ![staging-2020 ensembl org_entity-viewer_grch38_variant_21_10649835_rs1332086240_allele=0 view=transcript-consequences](https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-client/assets/6834224/9fc3bcd0-bdec-4b27-8cca-4488d341a1ae) Notice that the x-coordinate of the variant mark for a variant that starts at the first position of the CDS is 2, whereas we would expect it to be 0: ![image](https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-client/assets/6834224/dc39d5ed-8b51-44e4-9c41-0aabafeb6905) Investigation revealed several problems: - exon start/end coordinates were calculated incorrectly (start coordinate of every next exon in a CDS was the same as the end coordinate of the previous exon) - no distinction was made when creating a d3 linear scale between translating lengths into widths (minimum length is 0; max length is CDS length), and translating nucleotide coordinates into pixel coordinates (the lowest relative nucleotide coordinate is 1 and the highest is same as CDS length). It seems that two different d3 scales were required where only one was used. ## Related JIRA Issue(s) - https://www.ebi.ac.uk/panda/jira/browse/ENSWBSITES-2477 ## Deployment URL(s) http://ev-variant-fixes.review.ensembl.org

This current code, could got an errors with those flags: `-std=c2x -Wconstant-logical-operand -Werror` (on clang 16.0.0)

    if ((fmt == 2) || ((fmt < 2) && (LD2PT(vol) != 0))) {       /* Not an FAT-VBR or forced partition number */

    if ((fmt == 2) || ((fmt < 2) && (LD2PT(vol) != 0))) {       /* Not an FAT-VBR or forced partition number */

    if ((fmt == 2) || ((fmt < 2) && (LD2PT(vol) != 0))) {       /* Not an FAT-VBR or forced partition number */

author: jstone-lucasfilm
body:
This changelist adds support for color and unit transforms on the root nodes that are passed into shader generation, where previously they were only supported on non-root nodes in the material graph.

In MaterialX 1.38.9, a special-case pathway for root surface shader nodes was merged into the main logic, causing color transforms in some USD/MaterialX contexts to be omitted, and this changelist restores and generalizes the original approach to handle all root nodes.

author: ajshajib
body:
This PR adds a minimal version of the code that runs pPXF on spectra from a 3D datacube. The `squirrel_example.ipynb` provides an example of using this minimal version.

Main features added:

- class definitions to store data for 1D spectra, 3D datacube, Voronoi-binned and radially binned list of spectra,
- class definition to hold a template library,
- methods to call `log_rebin` and `ppxf` routines from the pPXF library and to Voronoi-bin with `vorbin`.

Thanks a lot to @shawnknabel for providing his codebase as a starting point for this PR! 🙏

author: jrockway
body:
Cluster metadata is stored in a new table with 1 row, enforced with a CHECK constraint.

I refactored `pfsdb.jsonMap` into `pgjsontypes.StringMap` so that a new `coredb` package can use it.

I adjusted InspectCluster to return the metadata, and added the `--raw` and `--output` options to the CLI so that you can inspect metadata you've added.

I added a new picker for clusters that just selects the current cluster; since pachd can't talk to other clusters, there is no need to be able to address them with pickers.  But having a picker made more sense than `cluster: true` or something.

Auth is handled with a new permission `EDIT_CLUSTER_METADATA` that is given to clusterAdmins.  If people want something like a `metadataOwner` role, we could add it, but I'm not sure if people want to delegate that responsibility.

author: gentoo-root
body:
Maintainer: @feckert
Run tested: armv7l, Netgear R7800, r23853-560965d582, tested by `mwan3 restart`

Description:

The awk expression in mwan3_delete_iface_rules splits the `ip rule list` output by spaces, therefore $1 contains the trailing colon (e.g., "1:", "1000:"). The < and > operators compare such values as strings instead of numbers, producing unexpected results (for example, "1:" > "1000").

Change the field separator to ":" for correct number comparison, so that the right rules are removed.

An example error message that may appear before the fix:

    Error: argument "1:" is wrong: preference value is invalid

It happens because `substr($1,0,4)` selects short numbers along with the colon. In other cases wrong rules may be removed, for example, if there is rule 10051, then rule 1005 will be removed.

body:
<!--
Thank you for submitting a pull request! Please provide a brief description of your changes below.
-->
### Description
This PR adds basic support for SCD2. Scope is defined [here](https://github.com/dlt-hub/dlt/issues/828#issuecomment-2016791397).

- Treats `scd2` as a special case of the `merge` write disposition.
- Support configurable names for the validity columns ("valid from" / "valid to").
- Validity column names default to `_dlt_valid_from` and `_dlt_valid_to` if the user does not specify names.
- Uses timestamps (not dates) to support sub-daily changes.
- Uses high timestamp (`9999-12-31T00:00:00+00:00`) in "valid to" column to indicate active records.
- Includes validity columns only in the root table. Validity dates for records in child tables can be linked through the root id.
- Does **not** use "standard" [configuration](https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/credentials/configuration) because it doesn't support resource-scoped configuration (correct me if I'm wrong). We want resource-scoped configuration because a user might want to load one table with the `scd2` strategy and another one with "regular" merge behavior, or use different validity column names for different tables.
- ~~Introduces `merge_config` argument on the `resource` decorator~~ Extends `write_disposition` argument such that it also accepts configuration dictionaries to let the user specify the merge strategy and validity column names..
- ~~Adds `merge_config` key to `TResourceHints`, but not to `TTableSchema`.~~
- Uses x-hints to store user configuration in the schema:
  - `x-merge-strategy` at the table level
  - `x-valid-from` and `x-valid-to` at the column level

-->

Introduces the `CpuControllerProcess`, a cpu isolator that is
implemented using cgroups v2 and indirectly exposed through the
`Cgroups2IsolatorProcess`. Hosts correctly configured for cgroups v2
that provide `cgroups/cpu` in the `isolation` flag and `cpu`
in the `agent_subsystems` flag will use this controller.

body:
This PR started off with the observation that I could still get an ASPECT in release mode that was compiled with a World Builder for which `NDEBUG` was not defined at compile time, which drastically slows down some algorithms inside World Builder. I think the fix for that is just `CMakeLists.txt:194`. However, I arrived at that only after a lengthy journey that was made harder by some other factors that I try to fix in this PR.
I changed:
- world builder 0.6 now switches off the same features independent of build type
- use `TARGET_COMPILE_OPTIONS` and `TARGET_COMPILE_DEFINITIONS` as much as possible and dont change `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`. @tjhei was there a reason we did this before?
- consolidate all compile options and definitions for the world builder in one part of the cmake file
- try to remove lines 558-560 which were meant as a stopgap until deal.II supported exporting compile definitions. recognized it was not working with 9.5.0 and opened dealii/dealii#16834. Left the lines in, but updated the comment.
- improved the detailed.log output to show output for all compile targets (debug and release) that are active

author: coreyostrove
body:
This PR covers changes intended to improve reporting support for two scenarios:

1. Report generation when using a CircuitListsDesign (addressing #320)
2. Report generation when performing GST without using gauge optimization. (addressing #412)

For item 1, previously it was the case that many plots, especially those related to model violation summarization had the assumption that the design has a PlaquetteGridStructure format hardcoded in. This of course makes sense for the model violation and TVD plaquette plots, but is an unnecessary assumption for the per-circuit histogram plots and other model violation statistics plots which would fail to generate. With the changes in this PR we can now generate all of the model violation plots that don't explicitly require this structure.

For item 2, this is in response to the bug report from @pcwysoc in #412. As reported there, when performing GST without gauge optimization the report generation would not create plots/tables related to gauge-variant quantities including distance metric tables, error generator plots, etc... This report reminded me that I ran into this exact same issue over a year ago in the context of generating reports for ModelTest protocols and fixed it on this branch (where I allowed it to subsequently languish after getting distracted). So I've now ported the fix I made for ModelTest over to the GateSetTomography protocol (and pre-emptively LinearGateSetTomography since this would have the same issue if anyone were to use it this w/o gauge optimization).

In the process of working on item 2 I originally implemented some changes to deprecate 'none' as an option, before reverting these changes upon the realization that the utility of having this option (beyond what is available using an empty GSTGaugeOptSuite) is that it allows for including no gauge optimization as an option among other gauge optimization suites (including multiple gauge optimizations in an estimate isn't something we do super often, but is fully supported). In going through this back and forth, however, it occurred to me (spurred on by the intuition about how the code worked that I'd gained from the other bugfixes) that there was going to be an edge case when using multiple gauge optimization suites when including 'none' as one of them wherein this would be skipped/not included in the report. Some subsequent testing confirmed this was indeed the case, with reports produced including all of the selected suites except for None. TLDR, I knew if I didn't fix this now I may never have done so, so I figured out a patch and that fix is included in this PR as well.

Unrelated change: While going through the gst protocol module I happened to noticed that the LinearGateSetTomography protocol was missing the auxfile specifications needed for directory-based serialization of the sort we have for GateSetTomography and StandardGST. So I added those (pattern matching off of the other two), which means that this protocol should be serializable now. Probably not a big deal either way, since I don't think many folks use this with any regularity, but figured I'd do it now since while it was fresh. I also added some new unit tests for all three of these protocols testing the directory-based serialization for each them.

About Us

Our Mission

Join us in our mission to keep our planet clean and green! Every day, countless tons of waste are improperly disposed of, polluting our air, water, and soil. By raising awareness and taking action, we can make a difference. Simple steps like recycling, reducing plastic use, and properly disposing of waste can have a huge impact. Let's work together to preserve the beauty of nature for future generations to enjoy. Together, we can make a difference!

Our Projects

Our projects focus on practical solutions for a cleaner environment. From community clean-up events to educational campaigns, we strive to make a tangible impact. Our recycling initiatives aim to reduce waste in landfills, while our tree planting drives enhance green spaces and combat climate change. Join us in these projects and be a part of the change you want to see in the world. Together, we can create a cleaner, greener future for all.

Get Involved

"Getting involved is easy! You can start by participating in our upcoming events, such as clean-up drives or tree planting activities. Join our community of volunteers who are passionate about making a difference. You can also support our projects by spreading awareness on social media or donating to fund our initiatives. Every small effort counts towards a cleaner, greener planet. Together, we can create a positive impact on our environment and inspire others to do the same. Join us today and be a part of the change!"
